name: Dinosaur Classification
description: Place each dinosaur in its correct order, suborder and family.

explain.suborder: Bipedal, hollow-boned carnivore: a classic theropod.
explain.family: Tyrannosaurids are large theropods with two-fingered forelimbs.

explain.suborder: Theropoda covers the bipedal carnivorous dinosaurs.
explain.family: Allosaurids are large Jurassic hunters with paired brow horns and three-fingered hands.

explain.order: Spinosaurus is a theropod and therefore saurischian.
explain.suborder: Despite the aquatic habits, its skeleton is fully theropod.
explain.family: Spinosaurids are semi-aquatic, sail-backed fish-eaters with crocodile-like snouts.

explain.suborder: Known mostly from snout fragments, but clearly theropod.
explain.family: Brazil's largest known theropod, a spinosaurid close to Spinosaurus; some researchers even treat it as the same animal.

explain.order: Velociraptor is a theropod, so it falls under Saurischia.
explain.family: Dromaeosaurids are small, feathered raptors with a sickle claw.

explain.suborder: A theropod, like every other raptor.
explain.family: The largest well-known dromaeosaurid: same sickle claw as Velociraptor, but roughly seven metres long.

explain.order: Small size does not change the hip: it is saurischian.
explain.family: Compsognathids are chicken-to-turkey-sized coelurosaurs with long tails and slender limbs.

explain.order: Saurischian, even though it had a backwards-pointing pubis convergent with ornithischians.
explain.suborder: A theropod that went herbivorous: the clade is defined by ancestry, not diet.
explain.family: Therizinosaurids are pot-bellied, feathered plant-eaters with the longest claws of any known animal.

explain.order: Sauropods like Diplodocus are lizard-hipped despite being herbivores.
explain.suborder: Sauropodomorpha groups the long-necked quadrupedal herbivores.
explain.family: Diplodocids are long-necked sauropods with whip-like tails.

explain.suborder: One of the heaviest sauropodomorphs ever found.
explain.family: A titanosaur: wide-gauge stance, sometimes armoured skin. Its exact family placement is still debated from fragmentary remains.

explain.order: Triceratops is bird-hipped, like all horned dinosaurs.
explain.suborder: Marginocephalia means 'fringed heads': frills and thick skull margins.
explain.family: Ceratopsids are horned dinosaurs with large neck frills.

explain.suborder: Thyreophora ('shield bearers') covers plated and armoured dinosaurs.
explain.family: Stegosaurids carry back plates and defensive tail spikes.

explain.suborder: Body armour places it with the shield bearers, alongside Stegosaurus.
explain.family: Ankylosaurids are armored tanks with a bony tail club.

explain.order: Duck-billed dinosaurs belong to the bird-hipped Ornithischia.
explain.suborder: Ornithopods are unarmoured herbivores that could walk on two or four legs.
explain.family: Hadrosaurids are duck-billed herbivores; Parasaurolophus has a hollow head crest.
